name: ULN2004ADR
title: Seven-channel high-voltage, high-current NPN Darlington array with clamp diodes
summary: The ULN200xA and ULQ200xA parts each hold seven NPN Darlington pairs with open collectors, a shared emitter pin E and a clamp diode from every collector to a shared cathode pin COM, for switching inductive loads such as relay coils and solenoids. Each output is rated 500 mA and 50 V, and outputs may be tied together for more current. The family differs only in the input network: the ULN2002A has a 7 V Zener and 10.5 kΩ in series for 14 V to 25 V PMOS logic, the ULx2003A has 2.7 kΩ for TTL and 5 V CMOS, and the ULx2004A has 10.5 kΩ for CMOS running from 6 V to 15 V.

circuits.title: ULN2003A as inductive load driver
circuits.description: Three 3.3 V logic sources each drive a group of inputs tied together (1B-2B, 3B-4B, 5B-6B-7B), and the matching outputs are tied in the same groups so the channels share each coil's current. Each coil is modelled as an inductance in series with its winding resistance RCOIL, returned to the coil supply VSUP. COM goes to VSUP as well, so the internal diodes catch each coil's turn-off kick, and E goes to ground. The example covers 12 V to 48 V coil supplies and 20 mA to 300 mA per channel.

circuits.title: PMOS logic output to load
circuits.description: A PMOS output transistor with its source on VSS drives input 7B of a ULN2002A directly; its drain is the only connection to the input. Output 7C sinks current from an inductive load returned to the load supply V, and COM is tied to V so the clamp diode is across the load. E is grounded; the other six channels are unused.

circuits.title: TTL output to lamp loads
circuits.description: A TTL gate's totem-pole output (phase splitter Q1, pull-up Q2 with its series diode D1, pull-down Q3) drives input 7B of a ULN2003A or ULQ2003A. All seven outputs carry a lamp returned to the supply V. COM is not tied to V: it goes through a switch marked lamp test to ground. E is grounded.

circuits.title: Buffer for higher current loads
circuits.description: A CMOS inverter output (Q1, Q2) on VDD drives input 7B of a ULN2004A or ULQ2004A. Output 7C drives the base of an external PNP transistor Q3 through R1, with R2 from the base to the supply V. Q3's emitter is on V and its collector feeds an inductive load to ground, with D1 reverse-connected across the load. COM is tied to V and E is grounded.

circuits.title: Pull-up resistor to raise drive current
circuits.description: A TTL totem-pole output (Q1, Q2, Q3) drives input 7B of a ULN2003A or ULQ2003A, with an added pull-up RP from VCC to the same node to raise the drive current. Output 7C drives an inductive load from the supply V; COM is tied to V and E is grounded.

circuits.title: Latch-up test circuit
circuits.description: One channel is switched by a pulse generator into its input while its output drives a 2 mH and 200 Ω load from the supply VS. An external 1N3064 diode runs from the output to VS, and COM is left open. CL, 15 pF to ground, includes the probe and fixture capacitance. VOH, the output level after switching, is specified with VS = 50 V and IO = 300 mA.

equations.name: Darlington current gain
equations.note: Measured with E grounded and COM open; II is held fixed for VCE(sat) and varied for hFE.

operation.text: Every channel is a two-transistor NPN Darlington. A series resistor RB feeds the base of the first transistor: 2.7 kΩ in the ULN2003A, ULQ2003A and ULN2003AI, 10.5 kΩ in the ULN2004A and ULQ2004A, and in the ULN2002A a 7 V Zener in series with 10.5 kΩ. A 7.2 kΩ resistor runs from the first transistor's base to its emitter, which is the second transistor's base, and a 3 kΩ resistor from the second base to E; the two act as pull-downs and limit leakage from the input. A clamp diode runs from each output to COM. Junction diodes from E to the input and from E to the output are part of the structure. All resistor values are nominal.

The Darlington connection multiplies the two current gains; the combined gain reaches about 10,000 A/A at some currents, so a small input current is enough for a large collector current. The ULx2003A works straight from TTL or 5 V and 3.3 V CMOS. The ULx2004A needs less input current than the ULx2003A and suits CMOS on 6 V to 15 V. The ULN2002A is meant for PMOS logic on 14 V to 25 V; its Zener and resistor keep the input current within a safe level.

With COM tied to the coil supply, the internal diodes suppress the kick-back voltage when a channel stops sinking: the energy stored in the coil drives a reverse current through the channel's diode into the coil supply.
A resistive load, or a pull-up resistor, is needed for the output to sink current and to have a high logic level. COM may be left open in this use.
Outputs can be tied together, with their inputs tied together, to sink more than one channel's 500 mA.

Each input and each output has a junction to E that is reverse biased in normal use. If one is forward biased, parasitic NPN transistors inside the die pull close to the same current out of nearby pins. The diode from collector to E is one of these structures and must not carry current; if a collector can swing below ground, an external Schottky diode clamps the undershoot.

The part has no supply pin. When COM is tied to the system supply, an output must not rise much above COM: the clamp diodes would then conduct hard and a large current into COM can damage the on-chip metal or overheat the die.

For a coil driver, settle the input voltage range, the temperature range, the output and drive current and the power dissipation. The low-level output voltage equals VCE(sat), given by the saturation curves. The number of coils that can be on together follows from the maximum-collector-current versus duty-cycle curves for the package, or more exactly from the power equations. Keep the junction below 125°C; junction temperature rises in proportion to on-chip dissipation.

Driving an Omron G5NB relay coil (2.8 kΩ) from 12 V with a 5 V input, the output falls from about 12 V to about 0.65 V at turn-on. At turn-off it rises to about 12.9 V, then drops to about 12 V between roughly 9 ms and 11 ms after the edge.

Input traces carry little current and may be thin; keep the input channels apart to limit crosstalk. Output traces should be wide enough for the load current, sized from the copper's current density. The common emitter trace carries the sum of all channels, up to 2.5 A in some designs, and should be very wide.
Propagation delays tPHL and tPLH are taken between the 50% points of the input and output edges.

ICEX is measured with the input open (or held at VI) and COM open; II(off) with a set collector current; II with the output open; VI(on) at VCE = 2 V and a set IC; IR across the clamp diode with VR from COM; VF with IF forced through the clamp diode.
